messages:
zoe: heads-up — after the kernel-selector overscan patch landed p95 host-side for tiny chats is up ~22ms. GPU work looks identical.

zoe: quick numbers from a short-chat perf run:
```
host_total_ms p50: 1.5  p95: 61 (+22)  p99: 84
parse/tokenize_ms p95: 13.8 (+11)
kernel_selection_ms p95: 2.4 (extra sync work)
stream_writev_calls p95: 3 -> baseline 1
kvcache_lookup_ms p95: 0.9
```

arun: overscan? that's the change that peeks more bytes to decide kernel/quant and nudges batch allocator prewarm, right?

frida: Yes. Overscan now inspects up to first 128 bytes synchronously to compute a fingerprint and prewarm kernels. That prewarm path runs inline in ingress.

zoe: Flamegraph excerpt shows ingress.read -> overscan_peek -> proto_unpack -> utf8_norm -> token_split -> token_adapter_legacy. Also a cluster of writev syscalls from the streaming chunker: many tiny frames instead of one coalesced writev.

frida: Why does overscan end up in legacy token adapter? We migrated hot paths to token_adapter_v3 months ago.

arun: The overscan fingerprinting uses an old suffix-match fallback for ambiguous metadata shapes. For tiny payloads it matches the fallback more often since it hashes a larger prefix and triggers some legacy heuristics.

tom: Repro steps I used: send 5 short prompts via grpc streaming with metadata X=small -> slow trace shows open("/usr/lib/icu/..."), and 2-4 writev calls per request. Strace shows additional mmap/open for ICU on slow runs.

perf-bot: rollback applied: reverted overscan CL 0f9b2a on canary at 07:18 UTC.

zoe: After rollback p95 fell back to baseline within ~6 minutes. KV hit rates, cache latency identical. This is host-side tokenization + framing overhead.

frida: Plan:
- move overscan fingerprinting off the critical ingress path (async or polling precompute)
- update fingerprint table to include the common grpc/http2 metadata shapes so we pick token_adapter_v3 for short chats
- change batch allocator prewarm to be best-effort (don't block request)
- make chunker prefer coalesced writev by default and only emit small frames when payload > 512B or explicit flush
- add e2e perf test for streaming short prompts asserting p95 host_total < 45ms

arun: Also add a cheap ascii-scan fast-path before utf8_norm in the overscan path to avoid ICU for ascii-only prompts. This can be done inline and is just a byte scan.

tom: I'll prep a canary with overscan disabled and writev coalescing enabled. Frida can update fingerprint table + allocator prewarm logic. Zoe will add perf test.

zoe: marking this P1 for Hosted, P0 for Dedicated (customers on pinned capacity reported tail latency). blame list: 0f9b2a -> 2c7e11 -> a4d9f0.

perf-bot: stateless-canary scheduled with overscan disabled and coalesce knob on at 07:40 UTC; collecting traces for 30m.

arun: FYI I dug into traces: when overscan runs it also increments a kernel-prefetch counter which causes a synchronous memmap of kernel blobs for some hosts — that memmap is cheap but the coupled ICU load is the killer. We should decouple prefetch from token selection.

frida: Agreed. Decouple and make prefetch lazy. Also add unit tests that simulate common small metadata shapes to assert token_adapter routing.

zoe: thanks all — paste traces here and I'll follow up with the PR link. :thumbsup:
